cards.text: In this song, David, who would later become king of Israel (2 Samuel 5:3), talks straight to God, and it's written for the choirmaster, with stringed instruments. The note at the top tells us the moment: the Ziphites, people from the town of Ziph in Judah (Joshua 15:55), went to Saul, king of Israel, and said, “Is David not hiding among us?” I spent YEARS in a junk drawer and NOBODY came looking for me, but David can't even hide without the locals handing out DIRECTIONS!

cards.question: David's hiding, and the Ziphites are tipping off Saul. What's the first thing David asks God for in this song?

answers.text: To save him by His name
To hide him from Saul's army
To give him strength to fight

cards.text: And David keeps knocking: “Hear my prayer, O God; listen to the words of my mouth.” That was me every time the drawer opened, yelling HELLO, DOWN HERE, STAMPER WITH A MUSTACHE!

cards.question: David begs God to hear his prayer and listen to the words of his mouth. Why is he pleading like this?

answers.text: Ruthless men are out to take his life
His own family has turned against him
He has fallen sick and can't get up

cards.text: David says these men have no regard for God. Then comes the word Selah, and right after it, this song turns a corner so sharp I almost slid off my gold base.

cards.question: After the Selah, David says God has left him to face these ruthless men alone.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Ruthless men are after his life, and David says, “Surely God is my helper; the Lord is the sustainer of my soul.” That's like the power going out and somebody calmly saying, “Relax, I know who's got the flashlight.”

cards.question: David calls the Lord the sustainer of his soul. What is David counting on God to do?

answers.text: Hold him up and keep him going
Make him famous across all Israel
Hand him the throne right away

cards.text: Now David turns to his enemies, and to who's going to deal with them. Lean in, friend, because this is the part of the group chat where everybody goes QUIET.

cards.question: David says he'll pay his enemies back himself.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: David says of God, “He will reward my enemies with evil.” Then he prays, “In Your faithfulness, destroy them.”
Then David stops talking about his enemies and makes God a promise. And unlike my promise to wipe the flour off this counter, he's actually gonna KEEP it.

cards.question: David turns from his enemies to the LORD. What does he promise to do for Him?

answers.text: Sacrifice freely and praise His name
Build Him a house of cedar
Fast and pray for forty days

cards.question: Back at the start, David asked God to save him by His name. Now David says he'll praise the LORD's name because it is good.

answers.text: True
False

cards.question: David closes his song by giving the reason for his praise. What does he say God has done for him?

answers.text: Delivered him from every trouble
Made him king over all Israel
Given him a city of his own

cards.question: In the last line, David says his eyes have looked in ___ on his foes.

answers.text: triumph
fear
sorrow
